chunks: The most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is salat (prayer), and it is the final counsel of the Prophets عليهم السلام. How excellent it is for a man to perform ghusl (ritual bath) or wudu (ablution), then complete the wudu thoroughly, then withdraw where no companion sees him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, looks upon him while he is bowing or prostrating. Indeed, when the servant prostrates and lengthens the sajdah, Iblis calls out: O woe to me! They obeyed Him while I disobeyed, and they prostrated while I refused.

key_terms.إِبْلِيسُ: Iblis, who laments his disobedience when seeing the servant's prostration
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), the most beloved deed to Allah in this narration
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), here with emphasis on completing it thoroughly
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: in the state of ruku', bowing in prayer
key_terms.سَاجِدٌ: in the state of sajdah, prostrating in prayer
key_terms.وَصَايَا: counsels or final instructions left by the Prophets
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلَ: to perform ghusl, ritual bathing before worship

ai.seo_question: Why is salat considered the most beloved deed to Allah, and what is the virtue of prolonged sajdah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that salat (prayer) is the most beloved deed to Allah عزّ وجلّ and that it was among the final counsels of the Prophets عليهم السلام. It praises ritual purity, sincerity in private worship, and prolonged sajdah, while portraying Iblis as lamenting the obedience of the worshippers in contrast to his own refusal.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.638 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The most beloved of deeds to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, is prayer. It is the final counsel of the prophets (as).
How beautiful it is for a person to perform ghusl (ritual bathing) or ablution (wudu'), perfecting it thoroughly, then to go to a place where no one can see him, and to humble himself before Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, in bowing (ruku') or prostration (Sujood). When a servant prostrates and prolongs his prostration, Iblis (Satan) cries out,
'Woe to me! They obeyed Him, while I disobeyed Him, and they prostrated while I refused.'".
